chapter: Chicago pioneers, community and New Orleans brotherhood
title: Tape interview of Elgar, and Erskine Tate still living
summary: Saunders has a taped interview of Elgar telling of Jabbo Smith's arrival and notes Erskine Tate lives down the street at about 85; DeMichael says the pioneers should be interviewed.

story.theme_name: Still working: current gigs, upcoming projects and plans
story.community_name: Hunting for old band photographs and scrapbooks

blocks.x: You mean, interview --

Interview things. A fellow was interviewing him. He wanted to write a book -- Cozy Cole and a lawyer called Danny Link in Cleveland, and he interviewed Mr. Elgar. And then he was telling him about the incidents
back in his day.
Very interesting.
Yeah, right, right. And I wished we could arrange -- I doubt if he'll talk, but he lived right down the street here, Erskine Tate. But he's an old man now. I guess he's --
He's still --

Yeah, he's still liv here, but I don't think he's too -- I mean, I know he's not active. But he lives right down the street here. And you know how it is, people can live right next door to you in a big city, you promise yourself you're going to go and see him or do something, you never do. You never get around -- time.
Well, this tape, do you have a copy of that tape, that interview?
I'll have to find it, I'll have to look it up, right. I'll have to look it up. I have a copy of it, right.
The Smithsonian might be interested in making a copy.

Right. Well, what I can do, I can look it up, and if I find it, I'll -- because it's here. But my things have been so disarranged. With me, I put things one place, and then the next thing I know my son comes in and rearranges everything and just disrupts everything, and then I
have to find it all --
(End of Side One.) END T2 S1
-- over again.
Well, I don't have that problem. I put things in certain places, and then I forget where I put them.
Yeah, that's true, too, I do that. Right.
That would be interesting. I'll pass the word along --

And he was talking in there. One of the things I remember in the tape, he was talking about Jabbo Smith, when he first brought him into Chicago, and how independent he was and all of this. It was a funny thing. I'll find that.
That's a real historical --
Right, right, piece.
Yeah. And Erskine Tate is --
Yeah, he's still living. Erskine has got to be about 85, close to 85.
I didn't realize that he was still living.
Yeah, he's still living, and he lives right down the street here somewhere. I would know about the house, where he lives.
There's a lot of the men who were in the development of jazz in Chicago. They're still around.
Yeah, I --
Should be interviewed (inaudible).
